findings.title: search_code bypasses skip/path filters on quoted or colon-containing paths
findings.why: git grep output is C-quoted by default (non-ASCII/control characters) and paths are then split at the first colon. The code uses that quoted/truncated string for is_skipped/glob_match but still returns the full match line. A PR can add e.g. `é.pem` matching a `**/*.pem` skip rule; the quoted path does not match the skip glob, so the file content is returned. Filenames containing `:` are also filtered against the wrong path. This violates the skip-rule contract and can leak files intended to be hidden.

findings.title: search_code has no file-size or output-size cap
findings.why: Unlike read_file, search_code never checks MAX_FILE_BYTES and appends whole git grep matching lines without truncation. A large text blob or a single very long matching line can produce arbitrarily large output, exhausting memory or the model context. One tool call can do this, so the 25-call budget does not help; this contradicts the claimed 200 KB limit applying to every tool.

findings.title: list_dir output is unbounded
findings.why: git ls-tree output is decoded and every entry is appended without a max entry count or byte cap. A repository/directory with very many files or very long names can make one list_dir call return a huge string and exhaust memory/context. The tool budget limits call count, not output size.

findings.title: read_issue lets JSON/KeyError escape instead of returning ToolError
findings.why: Only HTTPError, URLError and TimeoutError are converted to ToolError. A 200 response with malformed JSON, a non-object JSON value, or missing `title`/`state`/label keys raises JSONDecodeError/TypeError/KeyError. ToolBudget.wrap catches only ToolError, so such a response aborts the review instead of being returned to the agent as an error.

findings.title: Commit is not validated before being passed to git_log
findings.why: RepoTools stores any caller-supplied commit string, and git_log later appends it directly as an argument (line 168). If the value is not a full SHA, Git can interpret it as an option; e.g. `--output=/data/...` can write files, breaking the read-only guarantee. The constructor should enforce the same full-SHA validation used by MirrorStore.sync.

findings.title: Agent-controlled path_glob can cause regex cache growth or catastrophic backtracking
findings.why: _glob_regex is an unbounded global cache keyed by arbitrary path_glob strings, and its translation turns repeated `**/` into repeated `(?:.*/)?` groups. An agent can submit many unique or pathological globs, causing unbounded memory growth and potentially exponential backtracking in glob_match on long paths, hanging the review process.
